title: Battery communication fault
shortDescription: BMS is not responding to the controller.
fullDescription:
Error 10 on Segway-Ninebot scooters means the battery management system (BMS) cannot be reached on the internal data bus. Typical causes are a loose battery connector inside the deck or a BMS that has gone into sleep due to over-discharge.

A long rest on the charger can wake a deeply discharged battery. Persistent error requires opening the deck to inspect connectors.

fixSteps.title: Long charge
fixSteps.instruction: Leave charger connected for 4-6 hours to wake the BMS.

fixSteps.title: Inspect connector
fixSteps.instruction: Open deck plate and check battery-to-controller connector.

fixSteps.title: Service center
fixSteps.instruction: If BMS still unresponsive, have battery replaced.

whenToCallPro: If charging for several hours does not wake the scooter.

faq.a: Not always; deep discharge can mimic a dead battery.

title: Battery overvoltage
fullDescription:
Error 11 means the BMS has detected overvoltage, often during charging with a non-approved charger or after an internal cell failure.

Use only the original Segway-Ninebot charger. If the fault persists with the correct charger, the battery may need replacement.

fixSteps.title: Use OEM charger
fixSteps.instruction: Swap to original charger and retry.

fixSteps.title: Service check
fixSteps.instruction: If error continues, have battery tested.

whenToCallPro: If OEM charger still triggers the error.

faq.a: They can overcharge and start fires.

title: Battery undervoltage
fullDescription:
Error 12 indicates the battery is discharged below safe levels. Prolonged storage without charging is the most common cause.

Charge for several hours. If the battery cannot recover, it may be damaged.

fixSteps.title: Service if no recovery
fixSteps.instruction: If voltage still low, replace battery.

whenToCallPro: If charging does not restore voltage.

title: Battery temperature out of range
shortDescription: Battery too hot or too cold.
fullDescription: Error 14 protects the battery when temperature is outside safe range. Allow the scooter to reach room temperature before use or charging.

fixSteps.title: Bring to room temp
fixSteps.instruction: Let scooter sit indoors for 1-2 hours.

whenToCallPro: Only if persistent at moderate temperatures.

faq.a: Battery will act weak until warmed.

title: Motor Hall sensor error
fullDescription:
Error 20 indicates the controller cannot get consistent Hall sensor signals from the motor. Usually caused by a disconnected motor cable at the deck.

Check that the motor phase and hall plug is seated. Water ingress in the hub motor can also cause this.

fixSteps.title: Inspect motor cable
fixSteps.instruction: Open deck and reseat motor cable.

fixSteps.title: Dry hub motor
fixSteps.instruction: Let dry for 24 hours if moisture is suspected.

fixSteps.title: Replace motor
fixSteps.instruction: If hall sensors failed, replace hub motor.

title: Motor phase fault
shortDescription: One of the motor phase wires is disconnected or shorted.
fullDescription: Error 21 indicates a fault in the three-phase motor wiring. Check the motor plug for bent pins or a pinched cable.

fixSteps.title: Inspect connector
fixSteps.instruction: Open deck, check motor plug pins and wire.

fixSteps.title: Repair wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Replace damaged section or reseat pins.

whenToCallPro: If you are not comfortable with soldering.

faq.a: Possible; swap tested only at service.

title: Motor overcurrent
shortDescription: Motor drew more current than allowed.
fullDescription:
Error 22 is triggered when the controller detects an overcurrent event, often during a hard start on a steep hill or carrying an overweight load.

Restart the scooter. Recurring events indicate the motor or controller may be failing.
whenToCallPro: If it keeps happening under normal load.

title: Controller communication error
fullDescription: Error 30 indicates loss of data between the dashboard and the main controller. Usually a loose stem cable running up the tube.

faq.a: Yes, water in connectors is common.

title: Controller overheat
fullDescription: Error 31 appears when the scooter's speed controller overheats. Rest in shade and allow it to cool.
whenToCallPro: If it appears under light load.

faq.a: Avoid continuous full throttle on hills.

title: Brake lever fault
shortDescription: Brake lever sensor stuck or miswired.
fullDescription: Error 35 indicates the brake lever's sensor is reporting constant pressure (throttle cut-off), which prevents riding. Often caused by a bent lever, a stuck switch, or a waterlogged connector.

fixSteps.title: Free lever
fixSteps.instruction: Work the brake lever; clean around pivot.

fixSteps.title: Replace lever
fixSteps.instruction: Install new brake lever assembly if needed.

whenToCallPro: If wiring runs inside the stem.

faq.a: System blocks throttle when brakes are seen as applied.

title: Throttle sensor fault
fullDescription: Error 40 appears when the throttle returns implausible values, such as signal at rest. Typical causes are a damaged connector or a worn Hall throttle.

faq.a: No, it makes the scooter unusable.

title: IMU/tilt sensor fault
fullDescription: Error 45 relates to a fault in the internal IMU used on self-balance and some standing scooters. Sensor replacement is typically required.

faq.a: Sometimes the app can recalibrate; if not, replace.
